title: add surge protector: on-call backpressure controller and dynamic routing for pager storms
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Pager storms during external incidents or flappy downstream services cause on-call fatigue and large noisy alert volumes. Current tooling groups alerts but lacks a protective layer that temporarily throttles noisy channels, reroutes to overflow rosters, and applies short-lived aggregation rules without losing signal for SRE.

This PR introduces the 'Surge Protector' — an on-call backpressure controller implemented as an opt-in component in slo-toolkit. Goals: 1) reduce alert noise delivered to primary on-call during a detected surge, 2) preserve high-fidelity sampling of incidents for post-mortem, 3) provide safe automated routing and human-in-the-loop overrides, and 4) fall back gracefully to normal routing when conditions subside.

What this PR contains (summary checklist):
- [x] controller: backpressure decision engine with sliding-window rate heuristics and decay timer
- [x] policy CRD: SurgePolicy to configure thresholds, overflow rosters, aggregation windows, and TTLs
- [x] runtime hooks: safe temporary routing changes + annotation propagation for auditability
- [x] observability: surge_metrics, suppressed_alert_count, routing_actions counter and dashboards
- [x] tests: unit tests for controller logic, integration e2e simulating alert bursts, and chaos gating
- [x] docs: operator guide and runbook for manual escalation and override

Design highlights: the controller watches AlertEvent streams (ingest shim) and maintains a short-lived token-bucket per rotation-window that decays over time. When the bucket exceeds policy thresholds, the controller creates a SurgeRecord (ephemeral) and applies actions: 1) temporarily mute noisy channels (Slack/Email) for primary on-call and redirect to an overflow roster, 2) enable lightweight aggregation (coalesce alerts with same fingerprint for the window) while sampling 1:N raw events for diagnostics, 3) emit audit annotations to the original alerts and to a central SurgeLog index for RCA.

Safety and rollback: all routing changes are reversible and timeboxed by SurgePolicy TTLs. Manual overrides are supported via CLI and Console UI endpoints (this PR implements the backend endpoints and CLI wiring; Console UI follow-up tracked in ENG-1984). Actions are logged and include a rationale blob to make post-incident review straightforward.

Testing & CI: unit coverage added for decision boundaries and decay curves. An e2e scenario simulates a synthetic upstream flapping service producing 300 alerts/minute to validate suppression, sampling, and recovery. Load tests show the controller adds negligible CPU overhead (sub-2% at production scale) and reduces delivered notifications by ~78% in the simulated storm.

Rollout plan: staged rollout by customer namespace: opt-in annotation to enable. Default behavior is disabled. We will enable in Canary namespace for one week, then 10% of production namespaces, monitoring suppressed_alert_count, missed_ack_rate, and oncall_latency. Rollback can be immediate via feature flag.

Alternatives considered: integrate with existing alert aggregation service (rejected due to tight coupling risk) and push suppression entirely to downstream providers (rejected due to lack of sample preservation).

Related: ties into SRE-884 (oncall fatigue metrics) and ENG-1978 (alert routing policy unification). Docs added at docs/oncall/surge-protector.md.

Merge notes: squash merge, small API bump for policy CRD (non-breaking but requires operator reconciliation), documented migration steps in release notes.

release_notes: Add 'Surge Protector' on-call backpressure controller (opt-in). Operators can define SurgePolicy CRDs to automatically suppress noisy channels, route to overflow rosters, and sample raw events for RCA. Default disabled; staged rollout recommended. See docs/oncall/surge-protector.md for configuration and runbook.
notes_for_ops: Enable via annotation slo-toolkit.io/surge-enabled=true per-namespace. Configure SurgePolicy with TTL and overflow_roster. Monitor metric surge_protector.suppressed_alert_count and missed_ack_rate. Rollback by removing the annotation or setting policy.mode=disabled.
security_considerations: Controller preserves sampled raw events (1:N sampling) and emits an audit trail. Secrets not stored by controller; routing is enacted via the existing routing API. Security scan flagged no new concerns. Ensure RBAC for SurgePolicy is limited to operators teams.
